sources.title: Non-invertible Gauss law and axions

evidence.text: Higher gauging inserts symmetry-defect networks on a submanifold. For the specified discrete torsion, magnetic×winding 1-gauging produces a trivial closed condensation defect; imposing Dirichlet conditions on a boundary yields D^(1)_{p/N}. The authors use this construction to establish topologicality and determine defect actions.

evidence.text: Use twisted transition-function cocycles, fractional topological charges and commutators with electric symmetry generators. Their algebra with the Hamiltonian is used to infer equal-energy electric-flux orbits.

sources.title: Non-invertible Gauss law and axions

evidence.text: Dress anomalous symmetry operators with lower-dimensional TQFTs: the shift defect uses a 2+1-dimensional minimal Z_N TQFT, while the electric surface uses 1+1-dimensional Z_N gauge theory with compact scalar φ and U(1) connection c coupled to θ and F.

sources.title: Noninvertible symmetries and anomalies from gauging 1-form electric centers

evidence.text: Subtract Chern–Simons contributions from anomalous currents to obtain conserved charges, exponentiate them, and average over gauge-transformed operators. Fourier sums and Poisson resummation produce magnetic-flux selection conditions.

sources.title: Non-invertible global symmetries and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: Pass to a larger gauge group whose component and fundamental groups vanish as needed, then recover the original group by Higgsing while retaining the resulting magnetic defects.

sources.title: Non-invertible global symmetries and completeness of the spectrum

evidence.text: Retain the probe's internal QFT, match its anomaly against bulk inflow, and insert its partition function on the probe support. In axion electrodynamics the examples are a monopole worldline particle and a charged chiral boson on the string worldsheet.

sources.title: A Goldstone theorem for continuous non-invertible symmetries

evidence.text: Can an axial symmetry with a dynamical ABJ anomaly be represented by continuous non-invertible defects, and does a nonzero expectation value of a charged operator force a bulk gapless excitation? The paper also explores an application to massless string-theory form fields.

sources.title: The anomaly that was not meant IIB

evidence.text: Does the full discrete type IIB duality symmetry admit gauging on all allowed spacetime and duality backgrounds? The test concerns the quantum consistency of duality defects and background sums underlying the F-theory interpretation.

sources.title: Fermionic higher-form symmetries

evidence.text: How can invertible fermionic higher-form global symmetries act on extended operators, which tensor-spinor theories realize them, and what obstructs their gauging or preserves/breaks them under interactions and gravitational coupling?

sources.title: Three-form gauging of axion symmetries and gravity

evidence.text: How can nonlinearly realized anomalous Abelian symmetries be reformulated through three-form gauging, and what additional physics can undo axionic screening of strong CP, particularly through gravity?

sources.title: Emergent higher-form symmetry from type IIB superstring theory

evidence.text: Which invertible higher-form global symmetries emerge from gauging the type IIB duality group in its low-energy description, how can their operators measure 7-branes, and how do fermion parity and worldsheet orientation reversal modify them?

sources.title: Non-invertible symmetries in supergravity

evidence.text: Can higher-form symmetries apparently broken by supergravity Chern-Simons terms survive as non-invertible topological defects? The paper asks how to construct them, how they act on probe branes, and how dynamical objects remove them in the UV completion.

sources.title: Generalized Global Symmetries

evidence.text: Formulate higher-form global symmetries intrinsically through extended operators, and determine their consequences for selection rules, gauging, duality, spontaneous breaking, anomalies and phases of quantum field theory.

destinations.title: Should the quantum-gravity prohibition on global symmetry include fusion-closed non-invertible topological defects?

Does nonlinear dynamical gravity admit an electric one-form symmetry analogous to Yang–Mills center symmetry, and what are its charged operators, geometric defects, and conditions for explicit breaking?
